Title: Dream 7B: Powerful Open Diffusion LLM, Beyond Autoregressive | Product Hunt
# Dream 7B. ## Powerful Open Diffusion LLM, Beyond Autoregressive. Introducing Dream 7B, the most powerful open diffusion large language model to date. Matches/exceeds similar-sized AR models (LLaMA3, Qwen2.5). Excels at planning & offers flexible inference. Launch tags:Open Source•Artificial Intelligence•GitHub. No reviews yetBe the first to leave a review for Dream 7B. As an HKU alum, I'm incredibly proud of Dream 7B, a new language model from the HKU NLP Group & Huawei Noah’s Ark Lab. Watching a diffusion model like Dream 7B generate text is fascinating. Instead of the word-by-word output of standard autoregressive models, the text seems to emerge and refine itself all at once, almost like watching a dream form. It’s a unique feeling! While diffusion isn't the mainstream approach for language models yet, Dream 7B clearly shows the huge potential. It achieves performance comparable to top autoregressive models of its size and brings natural strengths in planning and flexible generation (like infilling or controlling the output order). They've released the model weights and code openly, which is fantastic. This really feels like a glimpse into exciting new possibilities for AI. Dream 7B seems like a solid step forward in language modeling. Flexible inference is a nice touch. i wish there was a way to test the model for non-techies. Dream 7B could revolutionize my productivity with its planning capabilities. How do you see it transforming workflows in your projects? I like the innovative planning features for complex tasks!

Title: Mercury: The First Commercial-Scale Diffusion LLM | Product Hunt
## The First Commercial-Scale Diffusion LLM. Mercury,from Inception Labs, is the first commercial diffusion LLM. Up to 10x faster than autoregressive models, with comparable or better quality on coding tasks. This is the 4th launch from Mercury. ## Mercury 3. The diffusion LLM that scaled 40x without slowing down. Mercury 3 is the most capable diffusion LLM released to date. It outperforms GPT-6 Luna and Claude Haiku 5.5 while running 4–8x faster at 1,000+ tokens per second. Launch tags:API•Artificial Intelligence•Development. Framer AI AgentsDesign and publish professional sites with AI. ## PreviousMercuryLaunches. Mercury Edit 2Ultra-fast next-edit prediction for coding. Launched on April 4th, 2026. Mercury 2Fastest reasoning LLM built for instant production AI. Launched on February 25th, 2026. MercuryThe First Commercial-Scale Diffusion LLM. No reviews yetBe the first to leave a review for Mercury. Mercury 3 is more than **40x** the size of Mercury 1, and it still generates at over **1,000 tokens/sec** on NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs. It's a diffusion LLM, generating and refining tokens in parallel instead of predicting them one by one. The context window has also grown from 260K to 1M tokens, with Inception reporting performance around GPT-6 Luna and Claude Haiku 5.5. Early partners are already using it for browser agents, real-time tutoring, search and customer support. A browser agent might call the model dozens of times for one task, so those seconds can add up quickly. It's available through an OpenAI-compatible API and OpenRouter. The browser-agent example is where the speed story gets interesting. I would be curious to see end-to-end task timings with the tool calls included. 1000 tokens/sec is wild 🔥 diffusion for coding feels like the right bet. 40x scale with no slowdown on a diffusion LLM is a serious claim, I'd love to see latency side by side with autoregressive models at the same quality. Big fan of the approach, good luck today.

results.title: Atlas: A World Model for Spatial Intelligence | World Labs
results.content:
Title: Atlas: A World Model for Spatial Intelligence | World Labs
September 1, 2026Introducing Atlas, our new omni world model for spatial intelligence. # Atlas: A World Model for Spatial Intelligence. World models generate, reconstruct, and simulate any possible world. At World Labs, we build these general purpose world models in pursuit of spatial intelligence. Today we are introducing Atlas, our next-generation world model. Atlas is an omni model that we pretrained from scratch to natively operate on text, images, video, and 3D. It is a multimodal autoregressive diffusion transformer: all inputs are combined into a shared spatial context. Atlas uses that context to generate what comes next, staying consistent in 3D with everything it has seen and imagining what lies beyond it. Atlas is built to scale: its performance improves with increased training compute, and we expect this trend to hold as we continue scaling. Atlas can perform a broad range of tasks spanning world generation, reconstruction, and simulation:. * **Camera-Controlled Generation**: Atlas generates images and videos from one or more images with pixel-perfect camera control, outputting up to 1 minute of video at 1440p. * **Spatial Reconstruction**: Atlas reconstructs real world scenes from one to dozens of input images. It generates both image frames from novel views and explicit 3D outputs, outperforming state-of-the-art models specialized for 3D reconstruction. * **Space-Time Simulation**: Atlas models space and time from input videos, reframing videos for dramatic visual effects and enabling Real-to-Sim workflows for robotics. * **Image Generation**: Atlas generates images and 360 panoramas from text; it can follow complex prompts, render text, and generate a wide variety of visual styles. Atlas takes one or more reference images and generates new views at any camera position and angle you specify. Generated views match the content and geometry of the input images, smoothly extrapolating beyond them to imagine parts of the scene not visible in the inputs. In the examples here, Atlas generates a complete scene from **a single input image**. It uses the content of the input image along with its broad world knowledge to imagine what the scene should look like from new angles. For example, you can place two unrelated reference images in the context and position them in 3D space; Atlas then generates a world that smoothly interpolates between them.
